gap: S7 — no simulator for Switch or Cover Calibrator

fixes.title: Switch and Cover Calibrator had no simulator at all, so flat-panel and power-switch flows could not be run without hardware
fixes.root_cause: Two separate holes, both required. (1) api/discovery.rs `drivers_for_device_type` omitted DriverType::Simulator for DeviceType::Switch and DeviceType::CoverCalibrator, so api_discover_devices never even asked the simulator scanner about them -- this is what produced the live log line 'Discovery complete for Switch: 0 devices'. (2) `scan_simulator_for_type` had no arm for either type, connect_simulator/disconnect_simulator/perform_simulator_health_check returned 'no simulator implementation', and all 20 DriverType::Simulator arms in ops/{switch,cover}.rs returned sim_gate::unsupported_simulator_device(). Note that fixing only (2) would have looked correct at the unit level and still discovered 0 devices in the app.
fixes.summary: Added SimulatedCoverCalibrator and SimulatedSwitch to bridge/src/api/devices/simulation.rs and wired both end to end (discovery driver list, simulator scan, connect/disconnect, heartbeat, and all 20 ops arms). Both are modelled to the fidelity bar rather than as Ok(constant): the cover is a POSITION (0.0 closed .. 1.0 open) travelling over SIM_COVER_TRAVEL_SECS, so it reports Moving en route, Unknown when halted part-way (it is genuinely on neither endstop, which is what a real controller reports after HaltCover), and Error once its own move timeout expires on a stalled lid -- which is what makes the previously-unreachable `state == 5` branch of the sequencer's wait_for_cover_state testable. Reversing mid-travel starts from the real current position, so closing a half-open lid takes half the time. The panel ramps its brightness over SIM_CALIBRATOR_SETTLE_SECS and reports NotReady on the way up AND the way down (ASCOM keeps a calibrator NotReady until it is safely off), so execute_calibrator_on's wait-for-Ready is a real wait; brightness outside 0..=255 is refused with an InvalidParameter rather than clamped. The switch models a Pegasus-style powerbox: two switched outputs, an adjustable output, two PWM dew channels and TWO READ-ONLY SENSOR CHANNELS, whose voltage and current are DERIVED from what is switched on (quiescent + bank + DSLR + dew duty x 0.03 A/%, with supply sag of 0.05 V/A) rather than stored, so a power dashboard wired to nothing cannot look alive. Booleans use the real ASCOM ISwitchV2 projection (true only when the value is in the upper half of its range), so a dew heater at 30% reads back false. Writes are accepted immediately but only become visible after SIM_SWITCH_SETTLE_SECS, reproducing the 'toggle, re-read, watch the control snap back' race a real status-polled controller creates. Out-of-range switch indices, out-of-range values and writes to read-only sensors are all errors, not clamps. Fault keys covercalibrator.command / covercalibrator.status / covercalibrator.cover / switch.command / switch.status are consulted by the new helpers, so SKOTIQ_SIM_FAULTS can jam a lid or kill a powerbox in a release build with no rebuild.
fixes.test_design: The cover tests go through api_discover_devices -> register_device -> connect_device -> skotiq_sequencer::DeviceOps (create_unified_device_ops), i.e. the exact path the OpenCover / CalibratorOn instruction nodes take, not the simulator helpers directly. The switch tests go through discovery -> connect_device -> the real DeviceManager::switch_* methods. This was deliberate: the defect was that discovery never asked for the simulator, so any test calling sim_switch_read() with hand-made arguments would have passed against zero discoverable devices.
fixes.revert_verification: Five independent severances, each run with `cargo test --package skotiq_bridge simulator_tests`, then restored. (1) Remove DriverType::Simulator from drivers_for_device_type for both types -> ALL 12 fail with 'discovery returned no simulated cover calibrator/switch'. (2) Restore that, replace all 10 cover.rs Simulator arms with an unsupported error -> the 6 cover tests fail, the 6 switch tests still pass (correct isolation). (3) Restore, delete only connect_simulator's DeviceType::Switch arm -> the 6 switch tests fail with 'no simulator implementation for device type Switch', the 6 cover tests still pass. (4) Restore, set SIM_COVER_TRAVEL_SECS / SIM_CALIBRATOR_SETTLE_SECS / SIM_SWITCH_SETTLE_SECS to 0.0 (every wire intact, devices merely instant) -> 4 fail, including 'the cover finished travelling before the command returned  left: 3  right: 2'. (5) Restore, make the current/voltage sensors stored constants and the boolean an independent `value > min` flag -> 'switching the 12V bank off left the reported draw at 0.4A (was 0.4A) - the sensor is not wired to anything' plus the ASCOM-projection test. All files restored from backup afterwards; full package re-run green.
fixes.verification: cd native/skotiq_native && cargo test --package skotiq_bridge -> 463 passed; 0 failed. cargo clippy -p skotiq_bridge --all-targets -> no warnings. rustfmt --check clean on all 7 files touched.
fixes.caveats: Four of the seven files touched are outside the stated ownership (api/discovery.rs, device_manager/{connection,heartbeat,mod}.rs) but none is another agent's assigned file and the fix is inert without them -- a simulator that is never discovered, never connectable and fails its heartbeat is not a simulator. Edits there are additive: two new match arms per dispatch site plus the two driver-list entries. device_manager/mod.rs also required REPLACING the test `switch_ops_simulator_always_errors_no_singleton`, which asserted the gap itself ('Switch has no simulator singleton in simulation.rs, so every op must loud-error'); its replacement pins the stronger contract (answers while connected, refuses while not) and takes the singleton test lock, which the original did not -- it was already racy against any test that connects the switch. NOT touched: device_manager/ops/sim_gate.rs (concurrently modified by the mount-slewing agent), so the new gates live in simulation.rs instead of alongside the other read_*/require_*_connected helpers; sim_gate's module doc still says switch and cover 'are NOT served by this module', which is now true for a different reason than it states. Also not updated: reports/coverage/simulator-fidelity-backlog.md item S7 (shared doc), and sim_faults.rs's doc list of example keys -- the new keys work without a code change because arm_from_env parses arbitrary keys.
